analysis.title: GS Basics - Capex Duration. Defensive Rotation. Record Share
key_insights: Asia AI complex sold off on 16 Nov: Taiwan -6%, Korea -3.6%, Nikkei -2.4%, with Advantest -11%, Lasertec -9%, Tokyo Electron -7%, Hynix -7.81% and TSMC -5.7%. Japan domestic consumer names rose 2.75% and healthcare 1.75%, while Japan beta fell 3.97% and high beta momentum fell 2.81%. The author reads AI as beta plus momentum.

The market treated last week's Nvidia move as a tactical redistribution of hardware market share. The author's concern is a larger second-order question: the duration of the whole AI capex cycle, and whether this is a rotation or the start of a digestion phase in aggregate AI enterprise capex.
Nominal yields moved multiple sigma higher last week and all three Treasury auctions reportedly tailed, signalling weak demand for duration. A tamer PPI made no difference to the selloff.

Credit held up well despite the violent rates move. The author's read is that reduced AI commitments hurt equity growth expectations but help credit as balance sheet risk falls: less spending, better credit, weaker equity multiples.

Prime book flows: fundamental strategies were up just over 1% and quant about 1.5% last week. Fundamental performance was largely beta driven and quant performance alpha driven. Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 2.6 pts (34th percentile over 1 year) with nets barely changed.

Overall prime book gross leverage was cut by 2 pts, with visible de-grossing in Asia and Europe. US flows were dominated by single stock shorting, partly offset by ETF covering. Hedge funds net sold US equities for a second straight week (5 of the last 6). ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in seven months.

UK: Burnham speaks ahead of the UK/EU summit, with the reset focused on trade, carbon markets and youth mobility. The Milburn review puts youth inactivity and welfare reform back in focus, but benefits will take time. Employment and CPI are the near-term catalysts. The backdrop is weak growth and employment against stubborn inflation.

France: the social security financing bill faces a Senate vote Wednesday after rejection in the National Assembly. The issue for OATs is whether any credible fiscal adjustment survives the parliamentary process, more than the vote itself.

Week ahead: Nvidia earnings Tuesday are unlikely to resolve the debate on future AI commitments. They probably reinforce that the stock is heavily discounted on next year's numbers, while the correct multiple for 2028+ is unknowable.

Week ahead: US retail sales Tuesday test consumer resilience, followed by retail earnings (HD Tuesday, TGT/LOW/TJX Wednesday, WMT Thursday). Watch trade down, margins and whether the defensive premium is justified. FOMC minutes Wednesday and Fed speakers including Williams and Warsh today matter given the rates repricing.
Geopolitics: watch possible Trump/Xi/Putin engagement at the APEC summit later in the week. Iran is on the agenda and Ukraine appears not to be. Expectations for progress are low.

Risk: semiconductors are approaching historical valuation lows while consumer staples carry large forward earnings premiums. Defensives would make sense if nominal and real yields were falling with growth, but they are not. Equities price a slowdown while rates price persistent inflation and restrictive policy. The author asks whether receiving rates is the better expression.

Sentiment is depressed, with the AAII bull/bear indicator near the low end of its range and CNN fear/greed similar, only beginning to recover. Positioning is the saving grace and likely drove last week's squeeze. With AI leadership under pressure, expensive defensives and little rate relief, the author sees no clear driver of a sustained recovery.

sector_views.rationale: Parts of the complex are approaching historical valuation lows, but AI leadership is under pressure from capex duration concerns.
Staples carry large premiums on forward earnings that are hard to reconcile with rates not falling, so the defensive premium looks hard to justify.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Tuesday. No EPS or revenue figures are cited. The author expects the print to leave the AI commitment debate unresolved and to reinforce that the stock is heavily discounted on next year's numbers.
Retail earnings this week: HD Tuesday, TGT/LOW/TJX Wednesday, WMT Thursday. Watch trade down, margins and whether the defensive premium is justified. No estimates are cited.

tension_points.bull_case: Last week's Nvidia move may be only a tactical redistribution of hardware market share, and positioning helped drive a squeeze. Semiconductors are near historical valuation lows.
tension_points.bear_case: The move may mark the start of a digestion phase in aggregate AI enterprise capex, which would weigh on equity multiples while helping credit.

tension_points.bull_case: Defensives make sense if growth slows and yields fall.
tension_points.bear_case: Nominal and real yields are not falling and staples carry large forward earnings premiums, so the defensive premium is hard to justify.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nominal and real yields falling alongside growth would support the defensive premium.
